wine.name: Bacharacher Hahn Riesling GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from Im Hahn, the core of the Hahn, a VDP.Grosse Lage of Bacharach
wine.sites: Im Hahn, the core of the Hahn at Bacharach, which the VDP ranks Grosse Lage: dark weathered Devonian slate facing south to south east, on slopes of 65 to 70 per cent above the Rhine. The wider Bacharacher Hahn around it, an Erste Lage, is the estate's monopole.
wine.making: Picked by hand, as the VDP requires of every Grosses Gewächs, and fermented dry. Falstaff's listings for several vintages give stainless steel for its maturing, and under the VDP's rule the wine is not released before September of the year after the harvest.
wine.glass: Wet slate and a wisp of smoke first, then white peach, tangerine and a hint of pineapple; dry and taut, with a firm line of acidity and a long, stony finish.
wine.ageing: Tight and stony on release, it gains depth over five to ten years and keeps well beyond that in a good vintage.
wine.serve: 10 to 13 degrees Celsius; no need to decant, though a young bottle opens with air in the glass; a white wine glass.

records.table: Toni Jost's Bacharacher Hahn Riesling GG comes from the core of the Hahn, steep slate above the Rhine at Bacharach that the family has worked for generations. Dry, taut and stony, it wants a cool pour rather than an icy one.
records.story: By the house's own account the Jost family has grown Riesling at Bacharach since 1831, and the estate, which also goes by the name Hahnenhof, has passed through seven generations of the family. In 1953 the Toni Jost estate of Bacharach joined with the Weller estate of Walluf in the Rheingau, through a marriage between the two families, and with it came vines in the Walkenberg at Walluf, a site the VDP ranks Grosse Lage. In 1987 seven Bacharach estates founded the VDP's Mittelrhein association, and the VDP has counted Toni Jost a member since that year. Under the VDP's classification the wider Bacharacher Hahn, an Erste Lage that the estate holds alone, surrounds a smaller core, Im Hahn, which the VDP ranks Grosse Lage, and the dry Grosses Gewächs comes from that core alone; later labels print its name. For a sommelier the wine is the Mittelrhein in one glass: Riesling, steep slate and the river, made dry and made to keep.

wine.name: Steeger St. Jost Riesling GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the St. Jost, a VDP.Grosse Lage above Steeg at Bacharach
wine.sites: The St. Jost above the hamlet of Steeg in a side valley at Bacharach, at 170 to 200 metres on a slope of about 60 per cent falling south: Devonian slate under windblown sand that the VDP traces to volcanic eruptions in the Neuwied Basin.
wine.making: Picked by hand, as the VDP requires of every Grosses Gewächs. By the account the house gave Vinous, its Rieslings are made in stainless steel with long, slow, spontaneous fermentations, and most are bottled late, towards the summer after the harvest; under the VDP's rule the GG is not released before September of that year.
wine.glass: White peach, apricot and ripe yellow apple over wet stone, with lime leaf and dried lemon peel; dry and firm, with lively acidity and a long, stony finish.
wine.ageing: Closed for its first few years, it opens after about five and lasts well beyond ten in a good vintage.
wine.serve: 10 to 13 degrees Celsius; no need to decant, though a young bottle opens with air in the glass; a white wine glass.

records.table: Ratzenberger's Steeger St. Jost Riesling GG grows on steep slate under a skin of windblown sand above Steeg, a hamlet in a side valley at Bacharach, and ferments slowly to dryness. Taut and stony when young, it opens with a few years in bottle; pour it cool.
records.story: The Ratzenberger estate works from Steeg, a hamlet of Bacharach set in a side valley off the Rhine, and works from a historic vaulted cellar. In 1987 seven Bacharach estates founded the VDP's Mittelrhein association, and the VDP has counted Ratzenberger a member since that year; from 1998 to 2010 the father of the house chaired it, and a later generation has since taken the cellar on. Among its Grosse Lagen at Bacharach are the Wolfshöhle and the St. Jost, which rises above Steeg, where the VDP describes Devonian slate lying under a skin of windblown sand. The house is known for a second craft as well: Riesling Sekt made by the traditional method, fermented in the bottle and left on its lees for years before disgorging, which turns the keen acidity of the gorge to sparkling wine. Its Rieslings are made in stainless steel, and by the house's account they ferment slowly with their own yeasts and are bottled late. For a sommelier the St. Jost Grosses Gewächs shows the dry face of a house whose cellar holds the region's two strengths, steep slate Riesling and Sekt.

records.table: Matthias Müller's Bopparder Hamm Mandelstein Riesling GG comes from the Mandelstein, steep slate in the Rhine's long loop at Boppard. Dry and fine, with lime, peach and wet slate, it rewards a few years in bottle.
records.story: By its own account the Müller family has farmed at Spay for about three hundred years, first as a mixed farm with vines on the steep hills above the Rhine. In the twentieth century the farm turned wholly to wine, and with each generation the vineyard grew, all of it in the Bopparder Hamm, the long loop of the river at Boppard. Shortly before 2000 the parents handed the estate to their son and his wife, and in 2007 it joined the VDP, whose Mittelrhein association seven Bacharach estates had founded in 1987; it is the association's one member from Spay. In the Hamm the house works the Feuerlay, the Mandelstein, the Ohlenberg, the Engelstein and An der Rabenlei, all on slate, and it makes them dry, off dry and sweet. Of all its wines the house names the Mandelstein Grosses Gewächs as the one it holds dearest, from its oldest parcel, directly below a wall. For a sommelier it is the Hamm's case for dry Riesling: steep slate in a bend of the river that faces the sun, made into a wine that keeps.

records.story: Weingart is a small family estate of Spay, on the Rhine by Boppard, where the family has farmed and grown vines since the early eighteenth century. It was long a mixed farm, and in the 1960s the parents of the present grower turned it wholly to wine. By the estate's own profile the son of the house, trained in viticulture at Geisenheim, took it on in 1996. Its vines lie mostly in three sites of the Bopparder Hamm, the Ohlenberg, the Engelstein and the Feuerlay, Riesling on steep slate, with some Spätburgunder beside it. Weingart has stayed outside the VDP, which in 2007 admitted its Spay neighbour Matthias Müller, so it labels its wines in the older German way: the vineyard, then the Prädikat, Kabinett, Spätlese or Auslese, then a word for dryness where the wine is dry. From the Feuerlay, a south facing slope of slate under loess loam, it makes Riesling dry, off dry and sweet. For a sommelier Weingart shows the Mittelrhein outside the VDP: a family grower whose labels speak the Prädikat language.

records.story: Lanius-Knab is a family estate of Oberwesel, on the Rhine between Bacharach and the Loreley, and by its own account the family has held it for about two hundred and fifty years. From 1991 a new generation of the family steadily enlarged the estate, and in 1995 it was admitted to the VDP. The VDP's Mittelrhein association had been founded in 1987 by seven Bacharach estates, and Lanius-Knab became its one member from Oberwesel. The house's vines lie in the Engehöller Bernstein and the Engehöller Goldemund and in the Oberweseler Oelsberg, a Grosse Lage, with Riesling taking well over three quarters of them and Spätburgunder and the white Burgundy varieties beside it. Within the Bernstein, which the VDP ranks Erste Lage, the parcel Am Lauerbaum is ranked Grosse Lage: a hollow like an amphitheatre that faces due south. From that parcel comes the Engehöll Grosses Gewächs, a dry Riesling. For a sommelier it is Oberwesel's answer to Bacharach: riper and fuller, yet a dry wine of slate all the same.

report: No wine labelled Oberweseler Engehöll Riesling was found. The house's dry Engehöll wines are Engehöller Bernstein Riesling (Erste Lage) and the Engehöll Bernstein Am Lauerbaum Riesling GG, which Falstaff lists for 2015 to 2023; the record teaches the GG and keeps the plan's words in its name.

Swap proposed for the checker: keep the house and the key and rename the pick's wine to Engehöll Bernstein Am Lauerbaum Riesling GG. The alternative is the house's Oberweseler Oelsberg Riesling GG, a Grosse Lage with its own GG; the Engehöll is kept here as the region record's choice.
The VDP ranks the Engehöller Bernstein Erste Lage on its site page, while the VDP's wine parcel page calls Bernstein am Lauerbaum a Grosse Lage; Falstaff's GG listings agree with the second.
The house claims its sites were ranked high in a Prussian classification of 1801; the left bank was French in 1801 and no second source was found, so the claim is left out.
The family's two hundred and fifty years are the house's own claim, and founded is left empty; a listing gives 1991, which is the handover, not a founding. The living head of the house is not named.
The glass rests on Falstaff's notes for the 2015, 2019, 2022 and 2023 (apricot, nectarine, peach, honey, slate, a sweet seeming core).
